notes: login() builds the SQL query via string interpolation of the raw email/password hash into a SELECT statement (loginAdminChallenge/loginBenderChallenge/loginJimChallenge)
Product search builds the SQL query via string interpolation of the raw search criteria into a SELECT statement, enabling UNION-based SQL injection (unionSqlInjectionChallenge/dbSchemaChallenge)
hash() uses MD5 for password hashing; used by every password check/set in the app
User model's password setter calls the MD5-based hash() from insecurity.ts (weakPasswordChallenge)
hmac() uses a hardcoded HMAC key ('pa4qacea4VK9t9nGv7yZtwmj') committed directly in source
generateCoupon() only base85-encodes the coupon (date + discount), with no HMAC/signature, so coupon codes can be reverse-engineered and forged (forgedCouponChallenge)

Redirect allowlist check uses substring match (url.includes(allowedUrl)) instead of exact/prefix match, letting an attacker embed an allowlisted URL inside a malicious redirect target (redirectChallenge)
Hashids salt ('this is my salt') is hardcoded, making the obfuscated hacking-progress continue-code trivially decodable (continueCodeChallenge)
TOTP secret is saved to the database in plaintext with no encryption at rest (twoFactorAuthUnsafeSecretStorageChallenge)
app.use(cors()) is enabled with no origin allowlist, so any origin can read API responses
/ftp is served via serveIndex with directory listing enabled (directoryListingChallenge)
/support/logs is served via serveIndex with directory listing enabled, exposing raw server log files (accessLogDisclosureChallenge)
errorhandler() dev middleware is wired in unconditionally (no NODE_ENV gate), returning full stack traces to clients (errorHandlingChallenge)
/metrics is exposed with no authentication or authorization check (exposedMetricsChallenge)

XML parser explicitly enables entity substitution and DTD loading (XML_PARSE_NOENT | XML_PARSE_DTDLOAD) together with filesystem input providers, enabling XXE-based file disclosure (xxeFileDisclosureChallenge/xxeDosChallenge)
Password-reset rate limiter's keyGenerator trusts the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header, letting an attacker bypass the limit by spoofing it per request (resetPasswordMortyChallenge)
Authorization middleware for PUT /api/Products/:id is commented out, leaving the route with no access control at all (changeProductChallenge)
Auto-generated REST resource for User excludes only password/totpSecret from client input; role is not excluded, so any authenticated caller can set role via POST /api/Users (registerAdminChallenge)

Review update matches only by client-supplied _id with no ownership/author check, and multi:true (line 20) lets one call bulk-update every review sharing that id (noSqlReviewsChallenge/forgedReviewChallenge)
Basket lookup by URL id returns the basket contents with no check that it belongs to the requesting user (basketAccessChallenge)
Data export trusts the client-supplied UserId in the request body instead of using the authenticated user's own id (dataExportChallenge)
fetch(url) makes a server-side request to an attacker-supplied URL with no scheme/host allowlist (ssrfChallenge)

Allowed-extension check runs on the raw filename before the poison-null-byte is stripped, so 'secret.bak%00.md' passes the .md check but resolves to secret.bak when served (forgottenBackupChallenge/nullByteChallenge)
User-supplied orderLinesData is executed via a vm-sandboxed eval (safeEval) — arbitrary code execution (rceChallenge/rceOccupyChallenge)
Uploaded YAML is parsed via yaml.load with no depth/size guard beyond a timeout; anchor/alias expansion can exhaust memory (yamlBombChallenge)
Valid test account credentials (testing@juice-sh.op) hardcoded in shipped client-side TypeScript (exposedCredentialsChallenge)

generateCoupon tool's discount cap ('maximum 10') exists only as a natural-language description in the schema, not as server-side validation — a prompt-injected chat message can drive the LLM to call the tool with an arbitrary discount (chatbotPromptInjectionChallenge/chatbotGreedyInjectionChallenge)
